thread:
kim-sales: FYI ACME wants a private POC in their VPC. No internet egress allowed. They prefer PrivateLink but asked for peering options too. Need a short handoff for networking + POC access. cc @raj_sre @diego-infra @taylor_re
raj_sre: Ok. Do we have their AWS account id and subnets? PrivateLink is usually easiest given strict egress rules.
kim-sales: Account 123456789012, two private subnets in us-west-2 (subnet-aaa, subnet-bbb). CIDR 10.10.0.0/16. They explicitly block IGW/NAT.
diego-infra: We can publish an Endpoint Service backed by an internal NLB in our VPC. They'll create interface endpoints in their account and we approve. We'll need the subnet IDs, desired AZs, and a contact for their infra team to approve connection requests.
taylor_re: Notes: interface endpoints don't require route table changes (they create ENIs). Customer must allow inbound 443 from their app subnets to the endpoint SG. We run TLS; we can require mTLS for the POC. Private DNS can be enabled on their endpoint to resolve api.redwood.internal -> endpoint.
kim-sales: They also asked about hostnames and certs. Can we provide a service name and instructions to enable Private DNS?
diego-infra: Yes. We'll provide service name and NLB SG. Example service name (test): com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-0abcde12345. NLB SG: sg-0ab1c2d3ef. They'll enable private DNS when creating the endpoint.
raj_sre: Steps for customer (interface endpoint flow):
- create interface endpoint in each AZ using subnets subnet-aaa subnet-bbb
- attach a security group allowing outbound 443 to our NLB SG and inbound from their app subnets
- enable private DNS for the service name
We approve the endpoint connection on our side. No IGW/NAT required.
kim-sales: What if they refuse any outbound 443 at all? They said egress is heavily restricted by policy.
taylor_re: If they block outbound to AWS services entirely, PrivateLink is usually still possible because it's an ENI inside their VPC that talks to our NLB — it does not traverse the Internet. But if their policy blocks all outbound traffic by default, they'd need to allow traffic to the NLB via the endpoint SG. Alternative is VPC peering + routing changes, but that still requires route updates and potentially DNS work. PrivateLink is the path of least resistance.
diego-infra: For peering path: we'll share the list of IPs to route (our target subnet range like 10.20.0.0/16). They must add routes in each route table: 
```
aws ec2 create-vpc-peering-connection --vpc-id vpc-0acme --peer-vpc-id vpc-0redwood --peer-owner-id 987654321098
# then accept and add routes like:
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-aaa --destination-cidr-block 10.20.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0abcd
```
But peering has DNS caveats and won't give hostnames automatically.
kim-sales: POC access: do we issue a hosted API key or prefer mTLS over PrivateLink?
taylor_re: For the PrivateLink POC we recommend mTLS. We can also provide a scoped hosted API key if they prefer to test quickly over the public API (but they'd need egress to public endpoints). For strict no-egress, PrivateLink + mTLS. We will provide a client cert bundle for the POC.
raj_sre: Checklist for handoff to customer infra:
- Provide service name (we'll send exact vpce-svc id)
- Provide NLB SG id (sg-0ab1c2d3ef) and the port we listen on (443)
- Customer creates interface endpoints in each AZ and enables Private DNS
- Customer sends endpoint IDs (vpce-0123, vpce-0456) so we can approve connections
- After approval, we exchange mTLS certs and test.
kim-sales: They also asked about data transfer and cost for PrivateLink during POC.
taylor_re: PrivateLink has AWS data processing fees per GB + standard cross AZ/transfer costs. Our Dedicated/Private pricing still applies (we bill usage for the POC). For initial POC we can offer credits — I'll loop in finance.
diego-infra: Quick sample CLI we can give them to create endpoints:
```
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint \
  --vpc-id vpc-0abcde123 \
  --vpc-endpoint-type Interface \
  --service-name com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-0abcde12345 \
  --subnet-ids subnet-aaa subnet-bbb \
  --security-group-ids sg-ccc111
```
They must pick SG that allows outbound 443 to our NLB SG and inbound from their application.
kim-sales: Also what about cross-account approvals — do we need an IAM role in their account?
raj_sre: Not for interface endpoints. They create the endpoint in their account and we approve the connection on our side. For peering there are different accepting flows and route updates.
kim-sales: Ok. Can we provide a short template email to send to their infra team with the needed info?
diego-infra: I'll draft one and include the service name, CLI snippet, SG recommendations, and the contact to send endpoint ids to.
deploy-bot: NLB (nlb-redwood-private-poc) created in us-west-2 internal subnets, target group ready. svc id com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-0abcde12345
kim-sales: Perfect. I'll send to ACME and request their subnet IDs + security contact.
taylor_re: I'll start a pricing note for finance and prep the cert bundle for mTLS.
raj_sre: Once they send vpce ids we can approve and kick off tests (curl + client cert). Example test:
```
curl --cert client.pem --key client.key https://api.redwood.internal/v1/health
```
kim-sales: Thanks all. Keeping this thread for the POC access window.
diego-infra: ping when they send endpoint ids.
kim-sales: will do :thumbsup:
